title: Why do I only see a short tool list?
goal: {{lena}} at {{vocab.org}} signs in to PingOne's hosted MCP server as an administrator and expects the full admin tool set. She sees a short list.
obstacle: The tool list is gated by the admin roles of the user who signs in. A short list looks like a broken server, so people debug the wrong thing.
control: {{mark}} checks the admin roles of the signed-in user first. Role gating is the control: a user with a read-only role never sees write tools, whatever the client asks for.

steps.title: Sign in as a viewer
steps.tell: Add the mock demo, press P1 login and sign in as mock.viewer (the password and code are filled in). The card tests the connection: the health card counts the tools and says in words that a short list usually means missing roles.
steps.say: The server is fine. The signed-in user is what the server is looking at.
steps.why: Role gating is per user, so the same server shows different tools to different administrators (Ping's MCP docs: the tools a user sees depend on their admin roles).

steps.title: Read the list
steps.tell: Open Tools. Every tool mock.viewer sees carries a read badge. No write tool is listed, so none can be called.
steps.say: No write tool in the list means no write path, not a hidden switch.
steps.why: A tool that is not listed cannot be called: this app also refuses a call to a tool the signed-in user does not see.

steps.title: Sign in as an admin
steps.tell: Sign out, then sign in again as mock.admin. The count grows and write and destructive tools appear, each labelled with why it was classed that way.
steps.say: Same server, same URL, a bigger list. Only the user, and so the roles, changed.
steps.why: The fix for a short list is a role assignment in PingOne, not a retry loop.

steps.title: Check the real numbers yourself
steps.tell: On a real tenant the count depends on the roles of the administrator who signs in. When this lab was built (2026-11-12, before the hosted server required a user sign-in) it listed 114 tools, including the MFA administration set. What a fully privileged administrator sees today is not verified by this app.
steps.say: I will quote a number only when I have measured it on our tenant.
steps.why: Numbers from a document are a starting point; the owner checks listed in docs/live-checks.md settle it.

proof.happy: The mock.viewer list contains read tools only; the mock.admin list contains write and destructive tools as well.
proof.blocked: Signed in as mock.viewer, a call to a write tool is refused because the tool is not in the list.

say: A short tool list is a roles question first, a server question last.
